academicJudgment.claimTested: UCR offers substantial computing, law, digital-ethics, misinformation and organizational study. Its strongest feasible combinations do not sustain the programme’s integrated study of cyber threats and crime: technical attack and defence, cybercriminal behaviour and victimization, digital investigation, and organizational incident response. General foundations and the real misinformation connection do not supply this continuing subject-specific inquiry. This judgment does not depend on the degree title, teaching language or professional role.
academicJudgment.finding: The new misinformation/deepfake course and real organizational/empirical study improve the positive response substantially. UCR networks, law, privacy ethics and policy also provide actual subject relationships. Nevertheless, neither whole taught composition sustains inquiry into cyber threats/crime across the confirmed technical protection, cyber-offender/victim, digital investigative and organizational response sequence. Combining general disciplines plus freely chosen cyber topics would assume subject teaching not supplied by those courses. This is a programme-level subject judgment, not a demand to reproduce every module or professional qualification.
academicJudgment.strongestObjection: This is an interdisciplinary social-science programme, not simply a hacking qualification. UCR actually teaches network/OS packet investigation, programming/software/algorithms, database authorization, general criminal and international/EU law, privacy/forensic-AI ethics, policy craft, digital publics, social psychology and empirical research. Calling Bullshit directly teaches misinformation/deepfake analysis and response. Organizational psychology provides actual culture/change, human-factor and research study. These are genuine academic connections, not merely transferable skills.
academicJudgment.coreChallenge: A claimed comparison of the full confirmed first 120 EC would still include the known cyber-specific subjects and integrated ransomware study. Excluding the unknown final 30 cannot remove these already-known defining requirements. Narrowing instead to general programming/law/methods plus misinformation would carve away known core substance rather than offer a meaningful comparison of that core. No numerical coverage threshold is used.

A correction to final-work format/access/weights changes full-degree certification, not this independent bounded negative.

readerValues.programmeDescription: Cybersecurity & Cybercrime at Leiden combines computing, governance, law and criminology to study digital security and crime. Students examine how networked systems work, how attacks occur, who commits and experiences cybercrime, and how organisations and public institutions can respond. Research methods, academic skills and multidisciplinary projects connect these perspectives.
